classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly requested cosine rule to the three given sides, obtain a radian angle, then use that angle to calculate the minor arc length.

content.prompt: A chord of length $5$ cm is drawn in a circle with centre $O$ and radius $2\sqrt{2}$ cm.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, below the stem and above part (a)
spec.description: Unshaded circle with centre O, two downward-sloping equal radii OA and OB, horizontal chord AB and the minor arc below it. Each radius is labelled 2√2 and carries one perpendicular tick; the chord is labelled 5.
spec.mathematics: OA = OB = 2√2 cm and AB = 5 cm. Endpoint coordinates are derived from cos(AOB) = -9/16; this derived angle is not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied labels and equality marks are visible; the angle and arc-length answers are hidden.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the cosine rule to find $\angle AOB$ in radians, correct to three decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta=\angle AOB$. By the cosine rule,
$$\begin{align*}5^2&=(2\sqrt{2})^2+(2\sqrt{2})^2-2(2\sqrt{2})(2\sqrt{2})\cos\theta\\25&=16-16\cos\theta\\\cos\theta&=-\frac{9}{16}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{9}{16}\right)\\\theta&\approx2.168\text{ radians}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, find the arc length cut off by the chord, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
Using the unrounded central angle from part (a),
$$\begin{align*}l&=r\theta\\l&=2\sqrt{2}\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{9}{16}\right)\\l&\approx6.13\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
